sections.content: How many people are "security guards and related occupations"?

170,430 people

were counted on the census as "security guards and related occupations" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Security guards and related occupations protect merchandise, individuals, hotels, offices, factories, shops, public grounds and private estates from injury, theft or damage.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "security guards and related occupations" there were more men than women (84.6% compared with 15.4%).

This means "security guards and related occupations" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "elementary administration and service occupations".

Men made up 84.6% and women made up 15.4% of "security guards and related occupations"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "security guards and related occupations" included:

  • printers
  • programmers and software development professionals
  • chartered surveyors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "security guards and related occupations" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "security guards and related occupations", 12.3% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "security guards and related occupations" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "security guards and related occupations" included:

  • metal machining setters and setter-operators
  • tailors and dressmakers
  • other skilled trades

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "security guards and related occupations" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "security guards and related occupations" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "security guards and related occupations", 10.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (79.8% compared with 20.2%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (92.6%) than self-employed (7.4%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
